title: The Rabbit Lands Encyclopedia
note: Search all entries by title, topic, material, tool or knowledge. Recipe, spell, book, map and skill pages use the installed game catalogues. The live server decides action eligibility and current prices.

skillNotes.attack: How hard you hit and how often you connect. The server rolls it; the client only shows what it said happened.
skillNotes.defense: How often a blow misses you, and how much of one your armour is allowed to soak.
skillNotes.harvesting: Train by gathering resources. Skill and recommended resource level affect success and timing; tools and carrying capacity also matter.
skillNotes.alchemy: Essences, bars, and the ingredients the rest of the trades are built out of.
skillNotes.magic: Spell unlocks, power and potency depend on Magic level and Magic nexus; family tomes and reagents can also be required.
skillNotes.potion: Everything that ends up in a vial, from the plain healing draught upwards.
skillNotes.summoning: Calling a creature to fight beside you, and the stones and flesh it costs.
skillNotes.manufacturing: Metal work: armour, weapons, and the plates and rings they are made from.
skillNotes.crafting: Rings, medallions and the small worked goods that need a mould.
skillNotes.engineering: Devices and traps, and the tools that build them.
skillNotes.tailoring: Thread, cloth, dye, and every garment made from them.
skillNotes.ranging: Train by ranged combat. Ranging increases maximum distance; shooting remains possible in melee with penalties.
skillNotes.overall: The server tracks overall experience and awards overall levels separately from individual skill levels.

categories.title: The World
categories.summary: Nymara, its hours and its weather
categories.intro: Rabbit Lands takes place on Nymara in the world of Eloria. The server owns world state and the game clock.

entries.title: What the server decides
entries.summary: Actions are checked by the server
entries.body:
The server decides movement, combat, inventory changes, harvesting and trades. The client displays those results and sends your requests.

The encyclopedia combines written guides with installed recipe, spell, book, skill and map catalogues. Those catalogues describe the client build; the live server still decides whether an action is allowed.

entries.title: Day and night
entries.summary: Six real hours to a Nymaran day
entries.body:
A full day is 360 game minutes. At ordinary clock speed one game minute is one real minute, so a Nymaran day lasts six real hours.

Daylight changes creature visibility as well as the scene lighting. See the Almanac tab for the date and current special day.
facts: The clock face on the lower HUD

entries.title: Marks and waypoints
entries.summary: The server's marks and your own
entries.body:
A waypoint is the server's: it appears on your map and reports the distance as you move.

A mark is your own. It never leaves this client, and it is drawn in a different colour so you can tell your own note from something the world told you.

entries.title: Weather and light
entries.summary: Rain, cloud, and the sky over each map
entries.body:
Weather belongs to the map you are standing on. The server states it, the client renders it, and it changes the light rather than only the picture.

An interior does not take the sky's weather. Walking indoors changes what lights you and what you can hear, which is why a doorway can feel like a different time of day.

entries.title: Night visibility and weather
entries.summary: Night changes which creatures you can see
entries.body:
Night reduces the distance at which ordinary creatures become visible. Perception and concealment can also affect visibility. A clear-looking road is not proof that no creature is nearby.

Weather is shared by players on the same map. Outdoor maps can have different weather profiles and changing conditions; interiors without a weather profile do not receive outdoor weather. The Almanac tab describes the current special day and any stated effects.

categories.title: Skills
categories.summary: The thirteen the server keeps for you
categories.intro: The server keeps a level and an experience total for each of these. The Statistics window shows all of them at once; the lower HUD shows the one you asked it to follow.

entries.title: Training skills
entries.summary: Practice, experience and recommended levels
entries.body:
Combat, harvesting, mixing and spellcasting award experience through their own server rules. The Statistics window shows your levels and experience. Spending pick points on attributes, nexus or perks is separate from training a skill.

Recipe levels are recommendations used in success calculations. A listed level does not guarantee a successful mix. Spell pages distinguish an unlock level from a recommended level. Consult the matching recipe or spell for materials, knowledge and nexus requirements.

categories.title: Combat
categories.intro: Combat is entirely the server's. This client asks it to start a fight and then reports what came back.

entries.title: Attacking
entries.summary: Three ways to start a fight
entries.body:
There are three ways to ask for a fight, and all three send the same request.

Hold Alt and click a living creature or player. The move icon on the lower HUD turns into the attack icon while Alt is held, so you can see what a click will do before you make it; let Alt go and it turns back.

Or click the attack icon on the HUD. That latches: the icon stays lit and every click attacks until you choose the move icon again, and holding or releasing Alt does not undo it.

Or select a target and press the attack key.

Whatever you choose, the server walks you into reach, decides whether the fight may start, and refuses the ones that may not.
facts: stays on until you pick the move icon

entries.title: Ranging
entries.summary: Range, reusable ammunition and close combat
entries.body:
Equip a ranged weapon and compatible ammunition or quiver. Maximum range starts at six tiles and increases by one tile for every ten Ranging levels. Perception improves damage and reduces distance loss.

You can keep shooting in melee, with reduced accuracy and damage. A distant hit can draw a creature towards you. Clicking the same target again stops shooting. The server resolves hit chance, damage, range and engagement.

entries.title: Armour and damage
entries.summary: Protection depends on the equipped piece and the attack
entries.body:
Equipment contributes the protection and modifiers shown in its item details and the Equipment window. Different attacks can deal physical or elemental damage; resistance and other effects can change the result.

Use the actual item details rather than judging protection by its appearance. Combat and damage are resolved by the server.

entries.title: How perks work
entries.summary: Pick points, tiers, exclusions and gear
entries.body:
A perk is bought with pick points, and most of them are bought more than once. There are 33 perks on the shelf and 33 of them come in tiers.

Pick points come from overall levels: two for each, spent on attributes, nexus or perks, and never spent twice. Every tier of a perk costs 3 pick points; most perks have three purchasable tiers, and Essence Keeper has five. Gold costs rise with each tier.

Some perks cannot be held together - Lucky Hitter and Lucky Dodger answer the same question from opposite sides, and so do Mirror and Life Stealing. The page for each perk says what it clashes with.

Worn gear can carry a perk. A cape does not simply grant one: it adds a tier up to the perk effect cap. Most perks need gear to reach tiers four and five. Essence Keeper can learn all five levels; its cape adds one level up to the 95% cap.

A removal stone takes back one tier and returns what that tier cost. At its highest tier a perk that says so can be switched off with the #perk command, which hands back the effect and not the pick points.

#list_perks names everything you hold, the tier you are at, and what that tier does.

categories.title: Harvesting
categories.summary: Taking things out of the ground
categories.intro: Everything the trades below are made from starts here.

entries.title: Harvesting
entries.summary: Nodes, levels, and why you stopped
entries.body:
The server controls which objects are resource nodes and what they yield. Resource requirements and your character determine whether gathering can proceed.

Click a node to start. The server reports when harvesting starts and stops. Moving, missing a tool, running out of space or another interruption can stop gathering. Search a resource name in the encyclopedia to find recipes that use it.
facts: clicking a node the server has described
moving, a full backpack, or the server

entries.title: Bags on the ground
entries.summary: What is dropped, and who may take it
entries.body:
Dropped goods appear in bags on the ground. Opening a bag requests its current contents from the server.

You must reach the bag tile to open it and pick up items. Other players can view the same bag. The server settles pickup requests and limits how much fits in your backpack and carrying capacity.

entries.title: Storage
entries.summary: What a storage keeper holds for you
entries.body:
Each character has storage held by the server. A storage keeper allows deposits and withdrawals. Use #storage view for a view-only preview from anywhere.

Withdrawals are checked against carrying capacity. The mixing window can draw materials from nearby storage; required tools must still be carried or equipped. Loot delivery and player payments can also involve storage, with the required approvals.

entries.title: Resource requirements
entries.summary: Levels, tools and yields
entries.body:
Resource definitions include a recommended Harvesting level, experience, a base gathering interval and, for some resources, a required tool. The live server controls the nodes and whether harvesting can start or continue.

Harvesting success and timing depend on the resource and your character. Some resources are ingredients in recipes; search their name across the encyclopedia to find uses. This client does not ship a complete per-resource location directory.

categories.title: Trade
categories.summary: Dealing with players and with the exchange
categories.intro: Two ways to move goods between people, both settled by the server.

entries.title: Trading and the exchange
entries.summary: Direct trades and the Nymara Exchange
entries.body:
A direct trade is between two players, and both must accept before anything moves. The server owns every step; the window shows what it has confirmed.

The Nymara Exchange takes listings and holds both goods and proceeds in escrow until they are collected.

entries.title: What a thing is worth
entries.summary: NPC prices, the exchange and player-set prices
entries.body:
NPC shop windows show their current buy and sell prices. Exchange listings and direct trades use their own offered prices. A recipe is a materials and requirements reference, rather than a market valuation.

Gauntlet loot can be assigned to individual players or split. The leader can set a price on eligible assigned items; payments use the storage approval flow before delivery. Personal rewards stay with their owner. Review quantities, prices and recipients before approving.

categories.title: Alchemy
categories.intro: Alchemy turns what is harvested into the essences and bars the other trades consume.

categories.title: Manufacturing
categories.intro: Metal work. Armour is made in pieces - helm, torso, legs, boots and shield - and the same bars go into the weapons that beat them.

categories.title: Crafting
categories.intro: Crafting wants a mould more often than it wants a fire.

categories.title: Engineering
categories.intro: Things that are built rather than forged.

categories.title: Potions
categories.intro: A potion is mixed once and drunk once. What it does is the server's to apply.

categories.title: Tailoring
categories.intro: The longest recipe list in the client, and the one that most often wants a book first.

categories.title: Summoning
categories.summary: Calling a creature to your side
categories.intro: A summoning is paid for in stones and flesh, and the creature that arrives is the server's, not yours.

categories.title: Magic
categories.summary: Sigils, spells and the effects they leave
categories.intro: Choose a spell family, targeting mode and Power 1–10. Higher power replaces separate greater spells.

entries.title: Casting and power
entries.summary: One effect, ten power levels
entries.body:
Learn the required spell-family tome, carry the reagents and choose a power your Magic level and Magic nexus support. Heal, Fire Bolt and Restore Ether need no tome. Higher power changes strength, duration or utility and can cost more ether and reagents.

The spell window can be searched and filtered by targeting mode. Generated spell pages list the unlock level, recommended level, base ether cost, nexus and Power 1 reagents. The live casting preview gives the exact cost at your chosen power.

entries.title: Self, Target, Allies and Burst
entries.summary: Choose who receives a spell
entries.body: A base name such as Heal affects you. Target selects one actor within 15 tiles; Bolt also means one target. Allies affects you and party or guild members within four tiles. Burst selects a location within 15 tiles and affects eligible actors within four tiles of it. Hostile spells respect party, guild and PK restrictions. Escape cancels target selection without spending resources.

entries.title: Damage, wards and Dispel
entries.summary: Match protection to the damage type
entries.body: Magic Bolt deals magic damage; Fire Bolt heat; Frost Bolt cold; Radiation Bolt radiation. Each has a Burst form and a matching ward. Elemental Ward combines heat, cold and radiation protection. Shield improves physical protection. Dispel removes poison, cripple, resistance reductions and drained stats. Magic Immunity temporarily blocks hostile spells.

entries.title: Transmute
entries.summary: Selected inventory items become gold
entries.body: Choose an inventory item and quantity. Review the required power and exact gold return before casting. Common items need Power 1, Uncommon 3, Rare 5, Epic 7 and Legendary 9. Their gold multipliers are 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 times the item base transmutation value. Only the selected quantity is consumed. Gold Coins and quest items cannot be transmuted.

entries.title: Recall and portal destinations
entries.summary: Higher power opens destination selection
entries.body: Recall at Power 1–4 returns you to Four Gates. At Power 5–10 choose a map with a portal entrance and the entrance where you will arrive. Maps with several entrances list each location. Blink remains a short teleport to a walkable place within 15 tiles.

categories.title: Books
categories.summary: What must be read before it can be made
categories.intro: A book is read once. Until the server records that you have read it, the recipes it teaches are refused however high your level is.

categories.title: Maps
categories.intro: Each region is its own map on the server. Crossing between them is a change of map, not a walk across a seam.

entries.title: Finding chat commands
entries.summary: Use #help for the current command list
entries.body:
Type #help or #list for the commands available to you on the current server. The Help tab lists local controls and commands handled by this client. A command beginning with # that the client does not handle is sent to the server.

Useful reference commands include #storage view for a view-only storage preview, #research for current research progress, #list_quests for quest numbers and #list_knowledge for knowledge numbers. Reset commands require a repeated confirmation and can remove progress: read the server response before confirming.
